title: Math: //, %, inf
short: Integer division, remainders, infinity and the math module.
what: Python ints never overflow, and a few number tools show up in almost every interview: // and % for whole-number division, float("inf") as a starting value for a minimum, pow with a modulus, and math.gcd, sqrt and ceil.
analogy: Sharing 7 sweets between 2 kids: each gets 7 // 2 = 3, and 7 % 2 = 1 is left over in the bag.

frames.label: 7 sweets, 2 kids
frames.say: / always gives a float. // divides and drops the remainder; % gives the remainder. divmod returns both.

frames.label: negative numbers
frames.say: With a negative, // rounds down toward minus infinity: -7 // 2 is -4, not -3. Then % is 1, never negative.

frames.label: cut toward zero
frames.say: To cut toward zero instead, as Evaluate RPN needs, write int(a / b). int(-3.5) is -3.

frames.label: inf = float("inf")
frames.say: inf = float("inf") is bigger than every number, a safe start for "best so far" when you want a minimum.

frames.label: powers
frames.say: pow(a, b, m) works out a ** b % m without building the huge number. "Answer modulo 10**9 + 7" wants this.

frames.label: int and round
frames.say: int() parses text and cuts floats toward zero. round() sends halves to the even neighbour: round(2.5) is 2.

frames.label: abs and math.*
frames.say: math has the rest. sqrt gives a float; isqrt the whole root. gcd is the biggest common divisor.

frames.label: round up
frames.say: Round up to count trips or pages: math.ceil(a / b), or stay in ints with (a + b - 1) // b or -(-a // b). All give 4.

when: Digits of a number with % 10 and // 10
python:
import math
print(7 / 2, 7 // 2, 7 % 2, divmod(7, 2))
print(-7 // 2, -7 % 2, int(-7 / 2))
best = float("inf")
best = min(best, 7)
print(best, float("inf") > 10**18)
print(2 ** 10, pow(2, 10, 7), pow(2, 100, 10**9 + 7))
print(int("42"), int(3.9), int(-3.9), round(2.5), round(3.5))
print(abs(-5), math.gcd(12, 18), math.sqrt(16), math.isqrt(17))
print(math.ceil(7 / 2), (7 + 2 - 1) // 2, -(-7 // 2))
n = 1234
print(n % 10, n // 10, 0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3)
watch: -7 // 2 is -4 in Python. To cut toward zero, use int(a / b).
float("inf") is a float. If no answer was found, return the -1 the problem asks for, not inf.
0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3 is False. Stay in integers, or compare floats with a small tolerance.
